title: Auxiliary Power Unit Mount — Aft Attachment Wear Inspection

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Wear inspection of the auxiliary power unit aft mount attachment, covering the bore, bush and bearing standards in service and the access route through the heat shield window where one is fitted.

sections.purpose: This task gives the wear inspection of the auxiliary power unit aft mount attachment for each of the three standards in service, and identifies which measurement applies to the standard fitted.
sections.job_setup_note: Three standards are in service and they are measured differently: the original aluminium link is measured at the bore, the steel link with plain bushes is measured at the bush inside diameter, and the spherical bearing is checked for radial and axial play. Reading the wrong measurement against the wrong limit is the most common error on this task. Where the heat shield window is fitted the shield stays in place; otherwise it must be dropped, which is most of the elapsed time.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm the mount standard from the configuration record and select the matching measurement. CAUTION: THREE MOUNT STANDARDS ARE IN SERVICE AND EACH HAS ITS OWN MEASUREMENT AND LIMIT. CONFIRM THE STANDARD BEFORE YOU MEASURE. 2. Open the tail cone access doors in zone 313. 3. Where the heat shield inspection window is fitted, remove the closing panel. Otherwise drop the aft heat shield. WARNING: SUPPORT THE HEAT SHIELD BEFORE THE LAST FASTENER IS REMOVED. IT IS AWKWARD AND IS REMOVED ABOVE HEAD HEIGHT. 4. Clean the attachment area and remove any oil residue. 5. On the original aluminium link, measure the bore at the two axes given in the figure. 6. On the steel link with plain bushes, measure the bush inside diameter at the two axes. 7. On the spherical bearing, check the radial and axial play with the dial gauge. 8. Record the measurement against the limit for the standard fitted. 9. Examine the bracket and the firewall panel around the attachment for cracking. 10. Examine the drain line clamp for security where the spherical bearing housing is fitted. 11. Refit the closing panel or reinstall the heat shield. 12. Close the tail cone access doors.
sections.close_out: Record the mount standard, the measurement taken and the limit applied. Report any attachment at or beyond its limit; on a high utilisation aircraft the wear rate is such that a measurement close to the limit will exceed it before the next scheduled inspection. Confirm the heat shield or its closing panel is refitted and torqued.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Step 3 uses the window on aircraft post MOD-149630 or post TTN-49-1020; otherwise the heat shield is dropped.

safety_precautions: Support the heat shield before the last fastener is removed.
Confirm the auxiliary power unit has been shut down for the cooling period.
Use the access platform; the attachment is above head height.
